title: How does CancellationToken flow through an ASP.NET Core application?
description: Request-aborted tokens end to end: EF Core, HTTP calls, task orchestration, and graceful shutdown.

data.text: **Question:** How does CancellationToken flow through an ASP.NET Core application?

ASP.NET Core creates one token per request — `HttpContext.RequestAborted` — which fires when the client disconnects (or the server initiates shutdown). The framework injects `CancellationToken` parameters into actions and minimal-API delegates automatically. Your job is **cooperative propagation**: pass that token down through every `await` that accepts one — EF Core queries, `HttpClient` calls, `Task.WhenAll`, channels — so abandoned requests release connections and threads instead of burning resources for a client that is already gone. Tokens also compose: `CreateLinkedTokenSource` merges request cancellation with your own timeout.

**Where it comes from:**
- MVC/minimal APIs bind a `CancellationToken` parameter to `RequestAborted` automatically
- Background jobs use the host's shutdown token instead — same pattern, different source
- Filters and middleware can wrap/replace tokens (e.g. per-request timeout policies)

**Propagation rules:**
- Pass the token into **every API that accepts one**: `ToListAsync(ct)`, `SaveChangesAsync(ct)`, `GetFromJsonAsync(url, ct)`, `WaitAsync(ct)`, `channel.Reader.ReadAllAsync(ct)`
- Propagate **deep**, not just one layer — a token stops at the first method that drops it
- For multi-step work, link tokens: `using var linked = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(requestAborted); linked.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));`
- Cooperative means loops must observe it too: `while (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)` or `ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` at safe checkpoints

**Behavior & semantics:**
- Cancellation is **cooperative**: nothing interrupts running code; the token only lets awaiting code throw `OperationCanceledException`/`TaskCanceledException`
- On client disconnect, EF cancels the query server-side (Attention signal in SQL Server), `HttpClient` aborts the request — the work stops, resources return
- Distinguish cancellation sources: `ct.IsCancellationRequested` (client gone / shutdown) vs a genuine timeout you created — log them differently. Client disconnects should not be 500s
- Don't pass `RequestAborted` into **work that must complete once started** (writing to a durable queue, sending a message) — use `CancellationToken.None` or a shutdown-only token there; the client leaving doesn't undo the side effect
- Wrappers: if you catch `OperationCanceledException`, rethrow when it matches your token — swallowing it fabricates success
- `HttpClient` timeouts are `CancelAfter`-style cancellation internally — same exception family

data.title: End-to-end propagation with a linked timeout

data.text:
Interviewers want to assess:
- Knowing cancellation is cooperative and only works if the token reaches the I/O
- Automatic injection of CancellationToken in actions/delegates
- Linked tokens for request-cancel + own-timeout composition
- Nuance: side effects that must complete even if the client leaves

items: Accepting a token and never passing it downstream — the first missing ct wastes all the work
Swallowing OperationCanceledException and returning a fabricated success
Logging client disconnects as server errors — noise that hides real incidents
Cancelling mid-side-effect: charging a card or publishing an event under RequestAborted
Creating unlinked timeouts — request aborted but the downstream HTTP call keeps running
Blocking on async work (`Task.Wait`) — the token can't interrupt a blocked thread
What happens to an EF Core query already executing when the token fires?
Client disconnects after payment is charged — what should happen?
How do you test cancellation without really disconnecting the client?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: RequestAborted is injected into actions — pass it to every await that accepts one
Cancellation is cooperative: loops and I/O must observe the token
Link request cancellation with your own timeouts via CreateLinkedTokenSource
Don't cancel irreversible side effects — choose the token deliberately
data.takeaway: A token is only useful where it travels: thread it through every layer, distinguish disconnect from timeout, and protect work that must finish.
